target: Jag vill förstå grammatiken på kvällen alltid.
english: I want to understand the grammar in the evening always.

target: Man borde läsa mer ibland nog.
english: One should read more sometimes probably.

target: Du behöver inte betala sedan länge idag.
english: You don't need to pay for a long time today.

target: Han kan inte sova ibland också.
english: He can't sleep sometimes too.

target: Vi ska ha fest i helgen också.
english: We are having a party this weekend too.
grammar: "I helgen" = this weekend. "Ha fest" = have a party — no article before "fest."

target: Hon får inte köra bil än dit.
english: She is not allowed to drive yet there.

target: Jag borde träna oftare sedan länge med familjen.
english: I should exercise more often for a long time with the family.

target: Vi måste lämna in rapporten under sommaren.
english: We must submit the report during the summer.

target: Han vill bo nära havet nästa vecka.
english: He wants to live near the sea next week.

target: Jag kan köra dig till flygplatsen dit.
english: I can drive you to the airport there.

target: Vi ska börja tidigt imorgon i helgen.
english: We are starting early tomorrow on the weekend.

target: Hon behöver en ny dator hela tiden.
english: She needs a new computer all the time.

target: Du borde prova det i biblioteket varje morgon.
english: You should try it in the library every morning.

target: Man får inte parkera här ibland nog.
english: You may not park here sometimes probably.

target: Jag kan inte lova något varje morgon.
english: I can't promise anything every morning.

target: Vi vill besöka Norrland på kvällen också.
english: We want to visit Norrland in the evening too.

target: Hon ska ha semester snart just nu.
english: She is going to have vacation soon right now.

target: Jag måste tänka på saken under veckan.
english: I must think about it during the week.

target: Du kan låna min bok på kvällen.
english: You can borrow my book in the evening.
grammar: "Låna" means both to borrow and to lend — context determines which.

target: Vi borde ses oftare varje dag i Sverige.
english: We should see each other more often every day in Sweden.

target: Han behöver inte komma efter jobbet till slut.
english: He doesn't need to come after work in the end.

target: Jag vill inte störa på kvällen verkligen.
english: I don't want to disturb in the evening really.

target: Man ska inte döma andra efter jobbet.
english: One shouldn't judge others after work.

target: Vi kan ta en promenad i helgen.
english: We can take a walk on the weekend.

target: Hon ska börja nya jobbet väldigt ofta.
english: She is going to start the new job very often.

target: Jag får vara med under sommaren egentligen.
english: I am allowed to join during the summer actually.

target: Du måste passa tiden väldigt ofta idag.
english: You must keep track of the time very often today.

target: Vi behöver diskutera detta i helgen idag.
english: We need to discuss this on the weekend today.

target: Han borde ta det lugnt förra veckan.
english: He should take it easy last week.

target: Jag kan inte bestämma mig förra veckan.
english: I can't decide last week.

target: Vi ska ha det trevligt för att kunna nå våra gemensamma mål snart.
english: We are going to have a nice time in order to reach our shared goals soon.

target: Hon vill bli bättre på svenska alltid.
english: She wants to get better at Swedish always.

target: Man måste respektera reglerna just nu alltid.
english: One must respect the rules right now always.

target: Du kan välja fritt varje dag alltid.
english: You can choose freely every day always.

target: Vi borde planera bättre i helgen väl.
english: We should plan better on the weekend I suppose.

target: Jag ska försöka mitt bästa under sommaren.
english: I will try my best during the summer.

target: Hon behöver tänka efter just nu idag.
english: She needs to think it over right now today.

target: Han måste opereras efter jobbet idag.
english: He has to have surgery after work today.

target: Jag vill aldrig glömma det här redan.
english: I never want to forget this already.

target: Vi kan lösa det här förra veckan.
english: We can solve this last week.

target: Du ska inte ge upp just nu.
english: You shouldn't give up right now.

target: Man borde njuta mer av livet med familjen.
english: One should enjoy life more with the family.

target: Jag behöver semester hela tiden idag.
english: I need a vacation all the time today.

target: Vi får se vad som händer på jobbet.
english: We'll see what happens at work.

target: Hon kan inte lova det hela tiden.
english: She can't promise it all the time.

target: Jag måste hinna med tåget under sommaren.
english: I must catch the train during the summer.

target: Vi ska göra det här tillsammans nog.
english: We are going to do this together probably.

target: Han vill inte prata om det idag.
english: He doesn't want to talk about it today.

target: Du borde berätta sanningen varje dag egentligen.
english: You should tell the truth every day actually.

target: Man får inte ge upp hoppet på kontoret.
english: One must not give up hope at the office.

target: Jag kan dansa salsa på kontoret varje morgon.
english: I can dance salsa at the office every morning.

target: Vi behöver varandra väldigt ofta idag.
english: We need each other very often today.

target: Jag tvättar mig varje morgon nästa vecka.
english: I wash myself every morning next week.
grammar: Reflexive verbs use "mig/dig/sig/oss/er/sig" — the action reflects back on the subject.

target: Hon klär sig snabbt nästa vecka redan.
english: She gets dressed quickly next week already.
grammar: "Klä sig" = get dressed. "Klä" without "sig" means to dress someone else.

target: Vi sätter oss vid bordet under sommaren.
english: We sit down at the table during the summer.
grammar: "Sätta sig" = sit down (reflexive). "Sitta" = to be sitting (non-reflexive).

target: Han rakar sig varje morgon på kvällen.
english: He shaves every morning in the evening.
grammar: "Raka sig" — reflexive verbs use sig (himself/herself/themselves) in 3rd person.

target: De lägger sig tidigt på kvällen ofta.
english: They go to bed early in the evening often.
grammar: "Lägga sig" = go to bed / lie down. Very common daily routine verb.

target: Jag känner mig trött under sommaren för alla.
english: I feel tired during the summer for everyone.
grammar: "Känna sig" = to feel (an emotion/state). Reflexive.

target: Hon gifter sig i sommar på kvällen.
english: She is getting married this summer in the evening.
grammar: "Gifta sig" (get married) is always reflexive. "I sommar" = this/next summer.

target: Vi bestämmer oss snart på kvällen varje dag.
english: We'll decide soon in the evening every day.
grammar: "Bestämma sig" (decide) — the reflexive pronoun matches the subject: mig, dig, sig, oss, er, sig.

target: Han skyndar sig till jobbet på morgonen.
english: He hurries to work in the morning.
grammar: "Skynda sig" (hurry) — many common Swedish verbs are reflexive where English isn't.

target: Jag kammar mig framför spegeln under sommaren.
english: I comb my hair in front of the mirror during the summer.
grammar: Daily routine verbs are often reflexive: kammar mig (comb myself), klär mig (dress myself).

target: Jag vaknar klockan sex just nu på morgonen.
english: I wake up at six right now in the morning.
grammar: "Vakna" is not reflexive in Swedish, unlike in some other languages.

target: Hon duschar i tio minuter sedan länge.
english: She showers for ten minutes for a long time.
grammar: "Duscha" = shower. Not reflexive in Swedish (unlike "tvätta sig" = wash oneself).

target: Vi äter frukost klockan halv åtta hemma.
english: We eat breakfast at half past seven at home.
grammar: "Halv åtta" = 7:30 (half TO eight). "Frukost" = breakfast.

target: Han borstar tänderna efter frukost varje morgon.
english: He brushes his teeth after breakfast every morning.
grammar: "Borsta tänderna" = brush teeth. No reflexive pronoun needed (unlike German/French).

target: Jag tar på mig skorna varje dag.
english: I put on my shoes every day.
grammar: "Ta på sig" = put on (clothes). Particle verb + reflexive.

target: Hon sminkar sig varje dag just nu.
english: She puts on makeup every day right now.
grammar: "Sminka sig" = put on makeup. Reflexive — she applies it to herself.

target: Vi förbereder oss för dagen under veckan.
english: We prepare ourselves for the day during the week.

target: Han dricker en kopp kaffe varje morgon.
english: He drinks a cup of coffee every morning.

target: Jag går hemifrån klockan åtta varje dag.
english: I leave home at eight every day.

target: Hon tar bussen till jobbet hela tiden.
english: She takes the bus to work all the time.

target: Vi börjar jobba klockan nio under veckan.
english: We start working at nine during the week.

target: Han tar lunchpaus klockan tolv under veckan.
english: He takes a lunch break at twelve during the week.

target: Jag äter lunch med kollegorna väldigt ofta.
english: I eat lunch with the colleagues very often.

target: Hon slutar jobba klockan fem på morgonen.
english: She finishes work at five in the morning.

target: Vi handlar mat på vägen hem varje dag.
english: We buy groceries on the way home every day.

target: Han lagar middag åt familjen på kvällen.
english: He cooks dinner for the family in the evening.

target: Jag diskar efter maten sedan länge nästa år.
english: I do the dishes after the meal for a long time next year.

target: Hon tittar på TV på kvällen gärna.
english: She watches TV in the evening gladly.

target: Vi promenerar med hunden förra veckan också.
english: We walk the dog last week too.

target: Han läser för barnen under sommaren varje dag.
english: He reads to the children during the summer every day.

target: Jag bäddar sängen varje morgon förra veckan.
english: I make the bed every morning last week.

target: Hon häller upp kaffe som en del av min dagliga rutin hemma.
english: She pours coffee as part of my daily routine at home.

target: Vi städar lägenheten på lördagar varje morgon.
english: We clean the apartment on Saturdays every morning.

target: Han stryker sina skjortor förra veckan gärna.
english: He irons his shirts last week gladly.

target: Jag tvättar kläder varannan dag förra veckan.
english: I do laundry every other day last week.

target: Hon dammsugare hela huset under sommaren på morgonen.
english: She vacuums the whole house during the summer in the morning.

target: Vi tar hand om trädgården på kvällen.
english: We take care of the garden in the evening.

target: Han matar katten hela tiden gärna.
english: He feeds the cat all the time gladly.

target: Jag går och lägger mig sedan länge.
english: I go to bed for a long time.

target: Hon somnar direkt på morgonen hemma.
english: She falls asleep right away in the morning at home.

target: Vi sover i åtta timmar varje dag.
english: We sleep for eight hours every day.

target: Jag sätter på larmet på morgonen ibland.
english: I set the alarm in the morning sometimes.

target: Han tar av sig jackan just nu.
english: He takes off his jacket right now.
grammar: "Ta av sig" = take off (clothes). Opposite of "ta på sig."

target: Hon torkar sig med handduken nästa vecka.
english: She dries herself with the towel next week.

target: Vi värmer upp maten förra veckan nog.
english: We heat up the food last week probably.

target: Jag kollar mejlen i affären varje morgon.
english: I check the email in the store every morning.

target: Han slappnar av i soffan under sommaren.
english: He relaxes on the sofa during the summer.
grammar: "Slappna av" = relax. A separable particle verb.

target: Vi myser framför brasan varje dag egentligen.
english: We cozy up by the fireplace every day actually.
grammar: "Mysa" = to cozy up. The verb form of "mysig" — quintessentially Swedish.

target: Jag tvättar ansiktet efter jobbet varje dag.
english: I wash my face after work every day.

target: Hon plockar undan hela tiden på kontoret.
english: She tidies up all the time at the office.

target: Vi gör i ordning allt på morgonen.
english: We get everything ready in the morning.

target: Han rastar hunden nästa vecka gärna.
english: He walks the dog next week gladly.
grammar: "Rasta" specifically means to take the dog out — not just any walk.

target: Jag klipper gräsmattan väldigt ofta här.
english: I mow the lawn very often here.

target: Hon vattnar blommorna under veckan gärna.
english: She waters the flowers during the week gladly.

target: Vi hämtar posten under veckan också.
english: We pick up the mail during the week too.

target: Han lämnar barnen på dagis ibland nog.
english: He drops the children off at daycare sometimes probably.
grammar: Dagis (daycare) is widely available and affordable in Sweden.

target: Jag tränar efter jobbet väldigt ofta varje vecka.
english: I exercise after work very often every week.

target: Hon yogar på morgonen varje dag egentligen.
english: She does yoga in the morning every day actually.

target: Vi lagar frukost ihop under veckan varje dag.
english: We make breakfast together during the week every day.

target: Han cyklar till jobbet varje dag dit.
english: He cycles to work every day there.

target: Jag dricker ett glas vatten på kvällen.
english: I drink a glass of water in the evening.

target: Hon medierar i tio minuter efter jobbet.
english: She meditates for ten minutes after work.

target: Vi tar en kvällspromenad på kvällen gärna.
english: We take an evening walk in the evening gladly.

target: Han skriver dagbok varje dag redan.
english: He writes in his diary every day already.

target: Jag lyssnar på en podd i helgen.
english: I listen to a podcast on the weekend.

target: Hon ringer sin mamma varje dag redan.
english: She calls her mom every day already.

target: Vi äter fika klockan tre under sommaren.
english: We have fika at three during the summer.

target: Han sorterar posten förra veckan väl.
english: He sorts the mail last week I suppose.

target: Jag häller upp ett glas juice till slut.
english: I pour a glass of juice in the end.

target: Hon ställer väckarklockan i parken varje morgon.
english: She sets the alarm clock in the park every morning.

target: Vi packar lunchlådor just nu under sommaren.
english: We pack lunch boxes right now during summer.

target: Han kör barnen till skolan under sommaren.
english: He drives the children to school during the summer.

target: Jag tar en dusch innan frukost gärna.
english: I take a shower before breakfast gladly.

target: Hon klär på sig vinterjackan nästa vecka.
english: She puts on her winter jacket next week.

target: Vi tvättar händerna före maten ibland hemma.
english: We wash our hands before the meal sometimes at home.

target: Han gör sin morgongymnastik under veckan också.
english: He does his morning exercises during the week too.

target: Jag äter en smörgås till lunch varje dag.
english: I eat a sandwich for lunch every day.

target: Hon dricker te innan sängs varje dag.
english: She drinks tea before bed every day.

target: Vi låser dörren på kvällen under sommaren.
english: We lock the door in the evening during the summer.

target: Han sätter på kaffebryggaren ibland verkligen.
english: He turns on the coffee maker sometimes really.

target: Jag duschar med kallt vatten just nu.
english: I shower with cold water right now.

target: Hon fönstrar sig innan hon går ut.
english: She checks herself in the window before going out.

target: Vi springer en runda varje morgon egentligen.
english: We go for a run every morning actually.

target: Han reder ut håret under veckan gärna.
english: He combs through his hair during the week gladly.

target: Jag brer smörgåsar åt barnen under veckan.
english: I make sandwiches for the children during the week.
grammar: "Bra smörgåsar" = make/spread sandwiches — literally to spread butter on bread.

target: Hon hänger upp tvätten på kvällen egentligen.
english: She hangs up the laundry in the evening actually.

target: Vi plockar ihop efter oss varje morgon.
english: We clean up after ourselves every morning.

target: Han förbereder mötet sedan länge varje vecka.
english: He prepares for the meeting for a long time every week.

target: Jag loggar in på datorn hela tiden.
english: I log in to the computer all the time.

target: Hon tar en rast efter jobbet gärna.
english: She takes a break after work gladly.

target: Vi umgås med grannen hela tiden med vänner.
english: We socialize with the neighbor all the time with friends.
grammar: "Umgås" means to socialize or spend time together — an important Swedish concept.

target: Han roar sig med ett spel dit.
english: He amuses himself with a game there.

target: Jag fördriver tiden med att läsa nu.
english: I pass the time by reading now.

target: Hon lägger sig klockan tio under sommaren.
english: She goes to bed at ten during the summer.

target: Vi vilar efter middagen ibland hemma.
english: We rest after dinner sometimes at home.

target: Han tar hand om sig själv gärna.
english: He takes care of himself gladly.

target: Jag njuter av morgontystnad hela tiden nog.
english: I enjoy the morning silence all the time probably.

target: Hon sträcker på sig hela tiden också.
english: She stretches all the time too.

target: Vi gör oss i ordning ibland egentligen.
english: We get ready sometimes actually.

target: Han tar av sig skorna inomhus gärna.
english: He takes off his shoes indoors gladly.
grammar: Taking shoes off indoors is a strict unwritten rule in Sweden.

target: Jag stänger av telefonen förra veckan alltid.
english: I turn off the phone last week always.

target: Vi slocknar framför TVn nästa vecka sedan länge.
english: We doze off in front of the TV next week for a long time.

target: Jag dricker inte kaffe sedan länge alltid.
english: I don't drink coffee for a long time always.
grammar: "Inte" goes after the verb in main clauses: subject + verb + inte.

target: Hon kommer inte idag just nu till slut.
english: She is not coming today right now in the end.
grammar: Main clause negation: subject + verb + inte. Simple and clear.

target: Vi har inte tid förra veckan gärna.
english: We don't have time last week gladly.
grammar: "Inte" after "har": "Vi har inte." Always after the finite verb.

target: Det regnar inte längre just nu ute.
english: It's not raining anymore right now outside.
grammar: "Inte längre" = no longer / not anymore. "Längre" = longer/anymore.

target: Han vill inte gå på kvällen snart.
english: He doesn't want to go in the evening soon.
grammar: With modal verbs, "inte" goes after the modal: vill + inte + infinitive.

target: Jag kan inte simma varje dag väl.
english: I can't swim every day I suppose.
grammar: "Kan inte" = can't. Negation always after the modal verb in main clauses.

target: Vi ska inte stanna länge i helgen.
english: We're not going to stay long on the weekend.
grammar: "Ska inte" = won't / aren't going to. "Länge" = for a long time.

target: Hon behöver inte komma ibland idag.
english: She doesn't need to come sometimes today.
grammar: "Behöver inte" = doesn't need to. Milder than "ska inte" (won't).

target: De har aldrig varit här under sommaren.
english: They have never been here during the summer.
grammar: "Aldrig" (never) goes in the same position as "inte" — after the verb.

target: Jag har ingenting att göra på kvällen.
english: I have nothing to do in the evening.
grammar: "Ingenting" = nothing. Also written "inget" in casual speech.

target: Det finns ingen hemma på morgonen här.
english: There is nobody home in the morning here.
grammar: "Ingen" = nobody/no one. "Inget" for ett-words, "inga" for plural.

target: Vi ser ingenstans en lösning hela tiden.
english: We see a solution nowhere all the time.

target: Hon sa ingenting sedan länge också.
english: She said nothing for a long time too.

target: Jag har inte sett honom just nu.
english: I have not seen him right now.
grammar: In perfect tense, "inte" goes between "har" and the supine: har + inte + sett.

target: Vi hade inte tid att vänta redan.
english: We didn't have time to wait already.

target: Han har aldrig ätit surströmming efter jobbet.
english: He has never eaten surströmming after work.

target: Det är inte mitt fel under veckan.
english: It's not my fault during the week.
grammar: "Mitt" = my (ett-word: "fel" is ett). "Min" for en-words.

target: Jag tycker inte om det förra veckan.
english: I don't like it last week.
grammar: "Tycker inte om" = don't like. "Inte" splits "tycker" and "om" (particle).

target: Vi vet inte var han bor med familjen.
english: We don't know where he lives with the family.
grammar: In subordinate clauses after "var/att/om": subject + inte + verb.

target: Hon sa att hon inte kunde komma.
english: She said that she couldn't come.
grammar: Subordinate clause word order: "att hon INTE kunde komma" — inte before verb.

target: Jag vet att han inte bor här.
english: I know that he doesn't live here.

target: Om du inte vill, behöver du inte.
english: If you don't want to, you don't have to.

target: Eftersom vi inte hade pengar stannade vi hemma.
english: Since we didn't have money we stayed home.

target: Jag hoppas att det inte regnar snart.
english: I hope it doesn't rain soon.

target: Det är inte sant efter jobbet nog.
english: It is not true after work probably.

target: Jag förstår inte vad du menar för alla.
english: I don't understand what you mean for everyone.

target: Vi kommer inte att vara sena nog.
english: We will not be late probably.

target: Hon tycker inte att det är svårt.
english: She doesn't think it's difficult.

target: Han bryr sig inte under sommaren i Sverige.
english: He doesn't care during the summer in Sweden.

target: De har inte bestämt sig än redan.
english: They haven't decided yet already.
grammar: "Än" (yet) goes at the end of negative sentences.

target: Jag har inte träffat henne förut redan.
english: I haven't met her before already.

target: Vi har varken tid eller pengar egentligen.
english: We have neither time nor money actually.
grammar: "Varken ... eller" = neither ... nor.

target: Hon gillar inte vinter varje dag ibland.
english: She doesn't like winter every day sometimes.

target: Jag var inte hemma igår under sommaren.
english: I was not home yesterday during the summer.

target: Vi kunde inte hitta vägen varje morgon.
english: We couldn't find the way every morning.

target: Han ville inte prata om det snart.
english: He didn't want to talk about it soon.

target: De behövde inte hjälp varje dag egentligen.
english: They didn't need help every day actually.

target: Jag fick inte svar nästa vecka till slut.
english: I didn't get an answer next week in the end.

target: Vi hann inte med tåget nästa vecka.
english: We didn't make it to the train next week.

target: Hon orkade inte mer väldigt ofta här.
english: She couldn't manage anymore very often here.
grammar: "Orka" = to have the energy/strength for something. Very Swedish.

target: Jag brukade inte gilla det sedan länge.
english: I didn't use to like it for a long time.

target: Vi borde inte ha gjort det nog.
english: We shouldn't have done it probably.

target: Han ska inte behöva vänta varje morgon.
english: He shouldn't have to wait every morning.

target: Det var inte så farligt under sommaren.
english: It wasn't that bad during the summer.

target: Jag vill inte ha något just nu.
english: I don't want anything right now.

target: Vi behöver inte oroa oss efter jobbet.
english: We don't need to worry after work.

target: Hon har inte ringt ännu varje dag.
english: She hasn't called yet every day.

target: Jag sa att jag inte visste redan.
english: I said that I didn't know already.

target: Det gör inte ont väldigt ofta på jobbet.
english: It doesn't hurt very often at work.

target: Vi har inte hunnit handla förra veckan.
english: We haven't had time to shop last week.

target: Han trodde inte sina ögon hela tiden.
english: He didn't believe his eyes all the time.

target: Jag ser inte problemet efter jobbet ibland.
english: I don't see the problem after work sometimes.

target: Vi har ingenting att klaga på nog.
english: We have nothing to complain about probably.

target: Hon vet inte vad hon vill verkligen.
english: She doesn't know what she wants really.

target: Jag märkte inte skillnaden ibland nog.
english: I didn't notice the difference sometimes probably.

target: Det spelar inte så stor roll varje dag.
english: It doesn't really matter every day.

target: Vi kan inte göra något åt det.
english: We can't do anything about it.

target: Han har inte ens försökt förra veckan.
english: He hasn't even tried last week.

target: Jag tänker inte ge upp väldigt ofta.
english: I'm not going to give up very often.

target: Vi fick inte plats på kvällen till slut.
english: We didn't get a seat in the evening in the end.

target: Hon hade inte hunnit äta varje dag.
english: She hadn't had time to eat every day.

target: Det regnade inte trots prognoserna på kvällen.
english: It didn't rain despite the forecasts in the evening.

target: Jag brukar inte klaga under sommaren på helgerna.
english: I don't usually complain during the summer on weekends.

target: Vi ska inte vara oroliga i helgen.
english: We shouldn't be worried on the weekend.

target: Han kunde inte sova hela natten med vänner.
english: He couldn't sleep all night with friends.

target: Jag ville inte störa förra veckan nu.
english: I didn't want to disturb last week now.

target: De kom inte i tid förra veckan.
english: They didn't arrive on time last week.

target: Vi har aldrig haft det här problemet.
english: We have never had this problem.

target: Hon tyckte inte om maten under sommaren.
english: She didn't like the food during the summer.

target: Jag visste inte att du var här.
english: I didn't know you were here.

target: Vi har inte råd med det väl.
english: We can't afford it I suppose.
grammar: "Ha råd med" = afford. "Inte" between auxiliary and main verb.

target: Han sa att han aldrig hade sett det.
english: He said he had never seen it.

target: Jag menade inte det så förra veckan.
english: I didn't mean it that way last week.

target: Det var inte alls dåligt förra veckan.
english: It wasn't bad at all last week.

target: Vi ska inte göra om det misstaget.
english: We won't make that mistake again.

target: Hon har aldrig klagat i helgen väl.
english: She has never complained on the weekend I suppose.

target: Jag trodde inte det var möjligt redan.
english: I didn't think it was possible already.

target: Vi hade inte planerat det nästa vecka.
english: We hadn't planned it next week.

target: Han förstod inte instruktionerna under veckan väl.
english: He didn't understand the instructions during the week I suppose.

target: Jag hittade inte det jag letade efter.
english: I didn't find what I was looking for.

target: Vi ska ingenstans ikväll hela tiden idag.
english: We're going nowhere tonight all the time today.

target: Hon sa att hon inte hade ätit.
english: She said she hadn't eaten.

target: Jag litar inte på det under sommaren.
english: I don't trust it during the summer.

target: De visste inte om det under sommaren.
english: They didn't know about it during the summer.

target: Vi har inte pratat om det ännu.
english: We haven't talked about it yet.

target: Han har inte svarat på mitt mejl.
english: He hasn't replied to my email.

target: Jag gillar varken kaffe eller te verkligen.
english: I like neither coffee nor tea really.

target: Vi har inte sett till henne väl.
english: We haven't seen her around I suppose.

target: Hon vägrar att inte vara med egentligen.
english: She refuses to not be included actually.

target: Jag kan inte tro att det hänt.
english: I can't believe it happened.

target: Vi lyckades inte lösa problemet efter jobbet.
english: We didn't manage to solve the problem after work.

target: Han lovade att inte göra om det.
english: He promised not to do it again.

target: Jag ser inte varför inte efter jobbet.
english: I don't see why not after work.

target: Vi har fortfarande inte fått svar egentligen.
english: We still haven't received an answer actually.

target: Hon kan absolut inte komma nästa vecka.
english: She absolutely cannot come next week.

target: Det finns ingen anledning att oroa sig.
english: There is no reason to worry.

target: Jag har inte minsta aning väldigt ofta.
english: I don't have the slightest idea very often.

target: Jag bor i Sverige vid sjön varje morgon.
english: I live in Sweden by the lake every morning.
grammar: "I" is used for countries and cities: "i Sverige," "i Stockholm."

target: Vi ses på måndag förra veckan gärna.
english: We'll meet on Monday last week gladly.
grammar: "På" is used for days: "på måndag," "på fredag."

target: Jag åker till jobbet under sommaren efter jobbet.
english: I go to work during the summer after work.
grammar: "Till" indicates direction/destination: "till jobbet," "till skolan."

target: Hon kommer från Umeå nästa vecka nog.
english: She comes from Umeå next week probably.
grammar: "Från" = from. Used for origin: "Jag kommer från..."

target: Vi bor på landet på morgonen med familjen.
english: We live in the countryside in the morning with the family.
grammar: "På landet" = in the countryside. "I staden" = in the city. Note the difference!

target: Han sitter på stolen i helgen i trädgården.
english: He sits on the chair on the weekend in the garden.
grammar: "På" for surfaces: "på bordet" (on the table), "på stolen" (on the chair).

target: Boken ligger i lådan under veckan gärna.
english: The book is in the box during the week gladly.
grammar: "I" for enclosed spaces: "i lådan," "i väskan."

target: Vi går till parken väldigt ofta efter jobbet.
english: We are going to the park very often after work.

target: Jag kommer från jobbet på kvällen snart.
english: I come from work in the evening soon.

target: Hon väntar på stationen på kvällen gärna.
english: She waits at the station in the evening gladly.
grammar: "På" for stations and stops: "på stationen," "på hållplatsen."

target: Vi bor i en lägenhet nästa vecka.
english: We live in an apartment next week.
grammar: "I" for dwelling: "bo i en lägenhet" but "bo på Vasagatan" (on a street).

target: Han jobbar på Volvo på morgonen här.
english: He works at Volvo in the morning here.
grammar: "På" for workplaces and companies: "jobba på Ericsson."

target: Jag studerar på universitetet under sommaren just nu.
english: I study at the university during the summer right now.
grammar: "På" for institutions: "på universitetet," "på sjukhuset."

target: Vi åker till stugan under sommaren på helgerna.
english: We are going to the cabin during the summer on weekends.

target: Hon bor i Göteborg sedan länge med familjen.
english: She lives in Gothenburg for a long time with the family.

target: De sitter i bilen förra veckan varje dag.
english: They are sitting in the car last week every day.

target: Jag springer i affären väldigt ofta nog.
english: I run in the store very often probably.

target: Vi handlar på ICA under veckan efter jobbet.
english: We shop at ICA during the week after work.
grammar: ICA is the largest supermarket chain in Sweden.

target: Han cyklar till skolan under veckan gärna.
english: He cycles to school during the week gladly.

target: Jag kom från ett möte varje morgon.
english: I came from a meeting every morning.

target: Vi bor på Vasagatan hela tiden just nu.
english: We live on Vasagatan all the time right now.
grammar: "På" for streets: "på Kungsgatan," "på Storgatan."

target: Hon går på bio på stranden varje morgon.
english: She goes to the cinema at the beach every morning.
grammar: "Gå på" for events and venues: "gå på bio," "gå på konsert."

target: Jag åker med tåg sedan länge ofta.
english: I go by train for a long time often.
grammar: "Med" for means of transport: "med buss," "med flyg," "med tåg."

target: Vi flyger till Barcelona varje dag egentligen.
english: We fly to Barcelona every day actually.
grammar: "Till" for destination with all transport: flyga till, åka till, gå till.

target: Han bor vid havet under sommaren i Sverige.
english: He lives by the sea during the summer in Sweden.
grammar: "Vid" = by/near: "vid havet," "vid sjön."

target: Jag väntar utanför dörren varje dag egentligen.
english: I wait outside the door every day actually.
grammar: "Utanför" = outside of.

target: Vi sitter innanför grinden på kvällen hemma.
english: We sit inside the gate in the evening at home.

target: Hon går genom parken under veckan väl.
english: She walks through the park during the week I suppose.

target: De bor nära centrum under veckan nog.
english: They live near the center during the week probably.
grammar: "Nära" = near. Can be preposition or adverb.

target: Jag står framför huset sedan länge hemma.
english: I stand in front of the house for a long time at home.

target: Vi sitter bakom scenen varje dag hemma.
english: We sit behind the stage every day at home.

target: Han bor ovanför oss ibland också.
english: He lives above us sometimes too.

target: Katten ligger under bordet på morgonen väl.
english: The cat is lying under the table in the morning I suppose.

target: Vi bor bredvid kyrkan på kvällen gärna.
english: We live next to the church in the evening gladly.

target: Hon springer runt sjön på kvällen efter jobbet.
english: She runs around the lake in the evening after work.

target: Jag går längs floden just nu efter jobbet.
english: I walk along the river right now after work.

target: Vi klättrar uppför berget efter jobbet varje vecka.
english: We climb up the mountain after work every week.

target: Han går nerför trappan på kvällen efter jobbet.
english: He walks down the stairs in the evening after work.

target: Jag åker förbi stationen under sommaren dit.
english: I drive past the station during the summer there.

target: Vi bor mittemot skolan hela tiden just nu.
english: We live across from the school all the time right now.

target: Jag pratar med min chef hela tiden.
english: I talk with my boss all the time.

target: Vi jobbar utan rast efter jobbet här.
english: We work without a break after work here.

target: Hon studerar för att bli läkare i Sverige.
english: She studies to become a doctor in Sweden.
grammar: "För att" = in order to. Used to express purpose.

target: Han gör det åt mig efter jobbet.
english: He does it for me after work.
grammar: "Åt" = for (someone's benefit): "Laga mat åt familjen."

target: Jag kom dit före henne på morgonen.
english: I got there before her in the morning.

target: Vi äter efter klockan sex sedan länge.
english: We eat after six o'clock for a long time.

target: Hon har bott här sedan 2020 redan.
english: She has lived here since 2020 already.
grammar: "Sedan" = since. Used with a point in time.

target: Vi jobbar under hela veckan förra veckan.
english: We work during the whole week last week.

target: Han reser mellan Stockholm och Malmö dit.
english: He travels between Stockholm and Malmö there.

target: Jag studerar om kvällarna varje dag här.
english: I study in the evenings every day here.
grammar: "Om" for recurring time: "om kvällarna," "om morgnarna."

target: Vi ses om en timme väldigt ofta.
english: We'll meet in an hour very often.
grammar: "Om" for future duration: "om en vecka," "om tre dagar."

target: Hon tänker på sommaren efter jobbet nästa år.
english: She thinks about summer after work next year.
grammar: "Tänka på" = think about. The preposition changes meaning: "tänka" alone = to think.

target: Jag drömmer om att resa hela tiden.
english: I dream about traveling all the time.

target: Vi pratar om vädret ibland på kontoret.
english: We talk about the weather sometimes at the office.

target: Han tittar ut genom fönstret ibland gärna.
english: He looks out through the window sometimes gladly.

target: Jag tror på dig på kontoret varje morgon.
english: I believe in you at the office every morning.

target: Vi litar på systemet i helgen gärna.
english: We trust the system on the weekend gladly.

target: Hon är bra på svenska just nu.
english: She is good at Swedish right now.
grammar: "Bra på" = good at. "Dålig på" = bad at.

target: De bryr sig om miljön i helgen.
english: They care about the environment on the weekend.

target: Jag väntar på svar efter jobbet gärna.
english: I'm waiting for an answer after work gladly.

target: Vi lyssnar på radio sedan länge på kvällen.
english: We listen to the radio for a long time in the evening.

target: Hon tittar på TV i trädgården på kvällen.
english: She watches TV in the garden in the evening.

target: Han skrattar åt skämtet sedan länge gärna.
english: He laughs at the joke for a long time gladly.
grammar: "Skratta åt" = laugh at. Note: "åt" here, not "på."

target: Jag ber om ursäkt förra veckan gärna.
english: I apologize last week gladly.

target: Vi bor i norra Sverige på morgonen.
english: We live in northern Sweden in the morning.

target: Hon åker till södra Frankrike varje morgon.
english: She goes to southern France every morning.

target: Han pratar i telefon sedan länge gärna.
english: He talks on the phone for a long time gladly.
grammar: "I telefon" (in phone) not "på telefon" — a common Swedish expression.

target: Jag sitter vid datorn efter jobbet hemma.
english: I sit at the computer after work at home.

target: Vi fikar på eftermiddagen på kvällen på kontoret.
english: We have fika in the afternoon in the evening at the office.

target: Hon arbetar på distans förra veckan gärna.
english: She works remotely last week gladly.

target: De bor utomlands sedan länge här.
english: They live abroad for a long time here.

target: Jag är hemma hos min syster nog.
english: I am at my sister's place probably.
grammar: "Hemma hos" = at someone's home.

target: Vi ses hos dig just nu sedan länge.
english: We'll meet at your place right now for a long time.

target: Han bor på en ö under sommaren.
english: He lives on an island during the summer.
grammar: "På" for islands: "på Gotland," "på en ö."

target: Jag sitter i solen ibland på jobbet.
english: I sit in the sun sometimes at work.

target: Vi väntar i regnet efter jobbet gärna.
english: We wait in the rain after work gladly.

target: Hon går ut i snön på kvällen.
english: She goes out in the snow in the evening.

target: Hunden springer efter bollen varje dag dit.
english: The dog runs after the ball every day there.

target: Jag skickar ett paket till dig till slut.
english: I send a package to you in the end.

target: Vi åker från Stockholm till Göteborg ofta.
english: We travel from Stockholm to Gothenburg often.

target: Hon bor ett stenkast från stranden här.
english: She lives a stone's throw from the beach here.

target: Han jobbar med data under veckan gärna.
english: He works with data during the week gladly.

target: Jag läser om svensk historia under veckan.
english: I read about Swedish history during the week.

target: Vi diskuterar under mötet under veckan också.
english: We discuss during the meeting during the week too.

target: Hon vandrar mot toppen nästa vecka under sommaren.
english: She hikes towards the summit next week during summer.
grammar: "Mot" = towards. Also means "against": "mot reglerna."

target: Vi kör mot norr förra veckan gärna.
english: We drive towards the north last week gladly.

target: Jag bor alldeles intill stationen i helgen.
english: I live right next to the station on the weekend.

target: Vi samlas kring bordet sedan länge här.
english: We gather around the table for a long time here.

target: Han lutar sig mot väggen varje morgon.
english: He leans against the wall every morning.

target: Vi åker med bil till Dalarna dit.
english: We go by car to Dalarna there.

target: Jag springer genom skogen efter jobbet ute.
english: I run through the forest after work outside.

target: Hon klättrar upp på berget hela tiden.
english: She climbs up the mountain all the time.

target: De bor mitt i stan varje dag.
english: They live in the middle of town every day.

target: Jag går bland träden under sommaren efter jobbet.
english: I walk among the trees during the summer after work.

target: Vi firar jämte varandra just nu redan.
english: We celebrate alongside each other right now already.

target: Han gömmer sig bakom gardinen ibland till slut.
english: He hides behind the curtain sometimes in the end.

target: Jag tittar över sjön förra veckan alltid.
english: I look across the lake last week always.

target: Vi promenerar bortom byn efter jobbet i Sverige.
english: We walk beyond the village after work in Sweden.

target: Hon sitter inne i huset under sommaren.
english: She sits inside the house during the summer.

target: De leker utanför skolan hela tiden ute.
english: They play outside the school all the time outside.

target: Vi bor nära naturen efter jobbet med familjen.
english: We live close to nature after work with the family.

target: Allt enligt plan sedan länge på kvällen.
english: Everything according to plan for a long time in the evening.

target: En stor bil under sommaren varje dag.
english: A big car during the summer every day.
grammar: En-words take the base adjective form: "en stor bil," "en fin dag."

target: Ett stort hus efter jobbet i skolan.
english: A big house after work at school.
grammar: Ett-words take -t: "stor" → "stort." "Fin" → "fint."

target: Stora bilar är populära i Sverige men de kostar mycket.
english: Big cars are popular in Sweden but they cost a lot.
grammar: Plural takes -a: "stor" → "stora." Same for both en- and ett-words.

target: Den stora bilen på morgonen för alla.
english: The big car in the morning for everyone.
grammar: Definite adjective takes -a AND needs "den/det/de": "den stora bilen." This is the double definite.

target: Det stora huset väldigt ofta hemma.
english: The big house very often at home.

target: De stora bilarna i helgen gärna.
english: The big cars on the weekend gladly.

target: Bilen är stor under sommaren redan.
english: The car is big during the summer already.
grammar: Predicate adjectives agree with the subject: "Bilen är stor" (en-word), "Huset är stort" (ett-word).

target: Huset är stort under veckan redan.
english: The house is big during the week already.
grammar: Simple definite: "Huset" = the house. Suffix -et for ett-words.

target: Bilarna är stora under sommaren redan.
english: The cars are big during the summer already.
grammar: Predicative plural: always -a form: "Bilarna är stora."

target: Hon är lång i affären varje morgon.
english: She is tall in the store every morning.
grammar: "Lång" = tall/long. Comparative: längre. Superlative: längst.

target: Han är stark efter jobbet gärna.
english: He is strong after work gladly.
grammar: "Stark" = strong. Regular comparison: starkare, starkast.

target: Barnet är litet hela tiden väl.
english: The child is small all the time I suppose.
grammar: "Liten" is irregular: liten (en), litet (ett), lilla/lilla (def.), små (plural).

target: De små barnen nästa vecka snart.
english: The small children next week soon.
grammar: "Liten" → "små" in plural. One of the most irregular adjectives.

target: En vacker dag förra veckan alltid.
english: A beautiful day last week always.
grammar: "Vacker" = beautiful. Becomes "vackert" for ett-words, "vackra" for plural.

target: Ett vackert landskap i helgen väl.
english: A beautiful landscape on the weekend I suppose.

target: Vackra blommor tillsammans i trädgården efter jobbet.
english: Beautiful flowers together in the garden after work.

target: Kaffet är varmt nästa vecka egentligen.
english: The coffee is hot next week actually.
grammar: "Varm" → "varmt" for ett-words. The -t makes it neuter.

target: Soppan är varm nästa vecka egentligen.
english: The soup is hot next week actually.

target: En kall vinterdag förra veckan också.
english: A cold winter day last week too.

target: Det kalla vattnet nästa vecka på kvällen.
english: The cold water next week in the evening.

target: Sverige är större än Danmark hela tiden.
english: Sweden is bigger than Denmark all the time.
grammar: Comparative: add -re. "Stor" → "större." "Fin" → "finare."

target: Stockholm är störst i helgen redan.
english: Stockholm is the biggest on the weekend already.
grammar: Superlative: add -st. "Stor" → "störst."

target: Hon är äldre än sin bror väl.
english: She is older than her brother I suppose.
grammar: "Gammal" → "äldre" → "äldst" — irregular comparison.

target: Han är yngre än mig just nu.
english: He is younger than me right now.

target: Det här är det bästa kafét väl.
english: This is the best café I suppose.
grammar: "Bra" → "bättre" → "bäst" — completely irregular.

target: Maten var sämre än väntat på kvällen.
english: The food was worse than expected in the evening.
grammar: "Dålig" → "sämre" → "sämst" — irregular.

target: Det är dyrare nästa vecka nog.
english: It's more expensive next week probably.

target: Malmö är mindre än Göteborg under sommaren.
english: Malmö is smaller than Gothenburg during the summer.

target: Det var den längsta dagen ibland egentligen.
english: It was the longest day sometimes actually.

target: En billigare lösning efter jobbet med familjen.
english: A cheaper solution after work with the family.

target: Den vackraste platsen just nu till slut.
english: The most beautiful place right now in the end.

target: En glad pojke i helgen dit.
english: A happy boy on the weekend there.

target: Ett glatt barn sedan länge snart.
english: A happy child for a long time soon.
grammar: "Glad" → "glatt" for ett-words. The -d changes to -tt.

target: Glada människor samlas i parken varje solig eftermiddag.
english: Happy people gather in the park every sunny afternoon.

target: Det är lättare att cykla på morgonen.
english: It's easier to cycle in the morning.

target: Det var den svåraste uppgiften nästa vecka.
english: It was the most difficult task next week.

target: En ny bok efter jobbet också.
english: A new book after work too.

target: Ett nytt jobb i skogen ibland just nu.
english: A new job in the forest sometimes right now.
grammar: "Ny" → "nytt" for ett-words. The -y gets doubled -t: "nytt."

target: Nya kläder kostar ofta mycket mer än man tror.
english: New clothes often cost much more than you think.

target: Den nya bilen i helgen med vänner.
english: The new car on the weekend with friends.

target: Hon är snabbare än jag på morgonen.
english: She is faster than me in the morning.

target: Han är den snabbaste löparen varje morgon.
english: He is the fastest runner every morning.

target: En rolig film på morgonen verkligen.
english: A funny movie in the morning really.

target: Ett roligt skämt förra veckan gärna.
english: A funny joke last week gladly.

target: Den roligaste filmen jag sett sedan länge.
english: The funniest movie I've seen for a long time.

target: En viktig fråga i helgen ute.
english: An important question on the weekend outside.

target: Ett viktigt beslut väldigt ofta med vänner.
english: An important decision very often with friends.

target: Viktiga möten hålls varje måndag morgon på huvudkontoret i centrum.
english: Important meetings are held every Monday morning at the head office in the center.

target: Sommaren är varmare än våren på kvällen.
english: Summer is warmer than spring in the evening.

target: Vintern är den kallaste årstiden nästa vecka.
english: Winter is the coldest season next week.

target: En hög byggnad varje dag egentligen.
english: A tall building every day actually.

target: Det högsta tornet just nu här.
english: The tallest tower right now here.

target: En tjock bok under veckan också.
english: A thick book during the week too.

target: Ett tunt papper under sommaren redan.
english: A thin paper during the summer already.

target: Det tunnaste tyget i affären ibland nog.
english: The thinnest fabric in the store sometimes probably.

target: En bred gata på morgonen för alla.
english: A wide street in the morning for everyone.

target: En smal väg under veckan alltid.
english: A narrow road during the week always.

target: Det är lika bra förra veckan också.
english: It's just as good last week too.
grammar: "Lika ... som" = as ... as. "Lika bra som" = as good as.

target: Hon är lika lång som sin syster.
english: She is as tall as her sister.

target: Det är inte lika kallt idag redan.
english: It's not as cold today already.

target: En mer intressant bok efter jobbet väl.
english: A more interesting book after work I suppose.
grammar: Long adjectives use "mer"/"mest": "intressant" → "mer intressant" → "mest intressant."

target: Den mest spännande filmen varje dag redan.
english: The most exciting movie every day already.

target: En gammal kyrka sedan länge i trädgården.
english: An old church for a long time in the garden.

target: Ett gammalt slott i parken varje morgon.
english: An old castle in the park every morning.
grammar: "Gammal" → "gammalt" for ett-words.

target: Gamla Stan i Stockholm ibland ute.
english: The Old Town in Stockholm sometimes outside.
grammar: "Gamla" is the definite/plural form of "gammal."

target: En ung kvinna nästa vecka med vänner.
english: A young woman next week with friends.

target: Det unga paret i helgen nästa år.
english: The young couple on the weekend next year.

target: En rik man på kvällen till slut.
english: A rich man in the evening in the end.

target: Ett rikt land varje dag redan.
english: A rich country every day already.

target: Rikare länder har ofta ett bättre utbildningssystem än fattigare.
english: Richer countries often have a better education system than poorer ones.

target: En fattig familj under veckan också.
english: A poor family during the week too.

target: Det fattigaste området sedan länge gärna.
english: The poorest area for a long time gladly.

target: En snäll granne nästa vecka just nu.
english: A kind neighbor next week right now.

target: Snällare barn brukar vara lättare att ha i klassrummet.
english: Kinder children tend to be easier to have in the classroom.

target: Den snällaste hunden just nu med vänner.
english: The kindest dog right now with friends.

target: En tyst kväll under veckan gärna.
english: A quiet evening during the week gladly.

target: Tystare än vanligt på stranden varje morgon.
english: Quieter than usual at the beach every morning.

target: Den tystaste platsen just nu alltid.
english: The quietest place right now always.

target: En ljus sommarkväll under veckan gärna.
english: A bright summer evening during the week gladly.

target: Det ljusaste rummet just nu verkligen.
english: The brightest room right now really.

target: En mörk natt på kvällen på kontoret.
english: A dark night in the evening at the office.

target: Mörkare dagar tillsammans under sommaren ibland.
english: Darker days together during summer sometimes.

target: Den mörkaste vintern efter jobbet just nu.
english: The darkest winter after work right now.

target: En ren skjorta i köket varje morgon.
english: A clean shirt in the kitchen every morning.

target: Ett rent kök under veckan gärna.
english: A clean kitchen during the week gladly.

target: Rena kläder hänger alltid i garderoben bredvid sovrummet hemma.
english: Clean clothes always hang in the closet next to the bedroom at home.

target: En smutsig bil väldigt ofta snart.
english: A dirty car very often soon.

target: Smutsigare än igår nästa vecka dit.
english: Dirtier than yesterday next week there.

target: En torr sommar just nu nog.
english: A dry summer right now probably.

target: Den torraste sommaren på länge sedan länge.
english: The driest summer in a long time for a long time.

target: En blöt dag på kvällen för alla.
english: A wet day in the evening for everyone.

target: Blötare väder väntas under nästa vecka enligt den senaste prognosen.
english: Wetter weather is expected next week according to the latest forecast.

target: En söt kattunge efter jobbet i skolan.
english: A cute kitten after work at school.

target: Den sötaste valpen förra veckan gärna.
english: The cutest puppy last week gladly.

target: En sur granne just nu varje dag.
english: A grumpy neighbor right now every day.
grammar: "Sur" means sour/grumpy. "Surare" = grumpier.

target: Han är gladare idag nästa vecka nog.
english: He is happier today next week probably.

target: Det är det bästa jag har ätit.
english: It's the best I have eaten.

target: En vänligare ton sedan länge till slut.
english: A friendlier tone for a long time in the end.

target: Det finaste väd er efter jobbet nu.
english: The nicest weather after work now.

target: En lugnare plats förra veckan väl.
english: A calmer place last week I suppose.

target: Det lugnaste jag vet förra veckan alltid.
english: The calmest thing I know last week always.

target: En starkare kaffe på kvällen gärna.
english: A stronger coffee in the evening gladly.

target: Det svagaste teet väldigt ofta med familjen.
english: The weakest tea very often with the family.

target: Billigast är det i januari väldigt ofta.
english: It's cheapest in January very often.

target: Jag har bott i Stockholm i fem år.
english: I have lived in Stockholm for five years.
grammar: Perfekt: har + supine. Group 3 verbs: bo → bott. Used for past with current relevance.

target: Hon har ätit lunch förra veckan nog.
english: She has eaten lunch last week probably.
grammar: "Äta" → "ätit" (supine). Irregular verb in Group 4.

target: Vi har aldrig besökt Kiruna varje morgon.
english: We have never visited Kiruna every morning.
grammar: "Kiruna" is Sweden's northernmost city — famous for the ice hotel and iron ore mine.

target: Han har jobbat hela dagen på morgonen.
english: He has worked all day in the morning.
grammar: Group 1 supine: -at. Jobba → jobbat.

target: De har rest till Norge nästa vecka.
english: They have traveled to Norway next week.
grammar: Group 2 supine: -t. Resa → rest.

target: Jag har läst den boken på morgonen.
english: I have read that book in the morning.
grammar: "Läsa" → "läst" (supinum). "Den boken" = that book (demonstrative use of "den").

target: Vi har köpt ett nytt hus väl.
english: We have bought a new house I suppose.
grammar: "Köpa" → "köpt" (supine). Past: "köpte."

target: Hon har skrivit ett brev väldigt ofta.
english: She has written a letter very often.
grammar: "Skriva" → "skrivit." Irregular Group 4 verb.

target: Han har druckit för mycket kaffe väl.
english: He has drunk too much coffee I suppose.
grammar: "Dricka" → "druckit." Irregular with vowel change.

target: Jag har gått till affären under sommaren.
english: I have walked to the store during the summer.
grammar: "Gå" → "gått" (supine). Irregular.

target: Vi har sett filmen efter jobbet väl.
english: We have seen the movie after work I suppose.
grammar: "Se" → "sett." Short and irregular.

target: De har kommit hem i skogen varje morgon.
english: They have come home in the forest every morning.
grammar: "Komma" → "kommit" (supinum). Swedish uses "har" for all verbs in perfekt (unlike German).

target: Hon har tagit bussen under veckan redan.
english: She has taken the bus during the week already.
grammar: "Ta" → "tagit." Irregular.

target: Jag har gett honom pengarna på kvällen.
english: I have given him the money in the evening.
grammar: "Ge" → "gett" (supinum). Short verb, short supinum. "Pengarna" = the money.

target: Vi har gjort allt vi kan nog.
english: We have done everything we can probably.
grammar: "Göra" → "gjort." Irregular supine.

target: Han har sagt sanningen nästa vecka väl.
english: He has told the truth next week I suppose.

target: Jag har aldrig varit i Japan väl.
english: I have never been to Japan I suppose.

target: Hon har hittat sina nycklar hela tiden.
english: She has found her keys all the time.

target: Vi har vunnit matchen efter jobbet redan.
english: We have won the match after work already.

target: De har förlorat passet under veckan redan.
english: They have lost the passport during the week already.

target: Jag har blivit sjuk varje dag redan.
english: I have become sick every day already.
grammar: "Bli" → "blivit." Extremely common in Swedish.

target: Vi har haft tur förra veckan gärna.
english: We have had luck last week gladly.
grammar: "Ha" → "haft."

target: Hon har fått ett jobb efter jobbet.
english: She has gotten a job after work.
grammar: "Få" → "fått."

target: Han har sovit länge efter jobbet väl.
english: He has slept for a long time after work I suppose.

target: Jag har sprungit fem kilometer under veckan.
english: I have run five kilometers during the week.

target: Vi har sjungit hela kvällen under veckan.
english: We have sung all evening during the week.

target: De har dansat hela natten hela tiden.
english: They have danced all night all the time.

target: Hon har lagat en god middag nog.
english: She has cooked a delicious dinner probably.

target: Jag har tvättat bilen på morgonen redan.
english: I have washed the car in the morning already.

target: Vi har städat hela huset varje dag.
english: We have cleaned the whole house every day.

target: Han har målat huset under sommaren nog.
english: He has painted the house during the summer probably.

target: Jag har flyttat tre gånger varje morgon.
english: I have moved three times every morning.

target: Hon har studerat i Lund varje morgon.
english: She has studied in Lund every morning.

target: Vi har firat midsommar under veckan gärna.
english: We have celebrated midsummer during the week gladly.

target: De har besökt Vasamuseet på morgonen redan.
english: They have visited the Vasa Museum in the morning already.

target: Jag har provat surströmming väldigt ofta nog.
english: I have tried surströmming very often probably.

target: Vi har vandrat i Kungsleden förra veckan.
english: We have hiked the King's Trail last week.
grammar: Kungsleden is Sweden's most famous hiking trail, 440 km through Lapland.

target: Hon har lärt sig svenska hela tiden.
english: She has learned Swedish all the time.

target: Han har ändrat sig efter jobbet nog.
english: He has changed his mind after work probably.

target: Jag har redan ätit väldigt ofta nog.
english: I have already eaten very often probably.

target: Vi har just kommit hem förra veckan.
english: We have just come home last week.
grammar: "Just" = just (now). Placed before the supine.

target: De har nyss gått ibland nog.
english: They have just left sometimes probably.
grammar: "Nyss" also means "just now" — interchangeable with "just" in many cases.

target: Hon har fortfarande inte ringt just nu.
english: She still hasn't called right now.

target: Jag har inte hunnit än under sommaren.
english: I haven't had time yet during the summer.

target: Vi har bakat kanelbullar i trädgården varje morgon.
english: We have baked cinnamon buns in the garden every morning.
grammar: "Baka" → "bakat." Group 1: all -at supine.

target: Han har byggt en altan under sommaren.
english: He has built a patio during the summer.

target: Jag har glömt mitt lösenord väldigt ofta.
english: I have forgotten my password very often.
grammar: "Glömma" → "glömt." Group 2 supine.

target: Hon har tappat sin plånbok nästa vecka.
english: She has lost her wallet next week.

target: Vi har beställt mat efter jobbet nog.
english: We have ordered food after work probably.

target: De har planterat blommor sedan länge nog.
english: They have planted flowers for a long time probably.

target: Jag har fixat problemet i skogen varje morgon.
english: I have fixed the problem in the forest every morning.

target: Han har sålt sin gamla bil redan.
english: He has sold his old car already.

target: Vi har rest runt i Europa väl.
english: We have traveled around Europe I suppose.

target: Hon har slutat röka på kvällen nog.
english: She has quit smoking in the evening probably.

target: Jag har börjat träna hemma hos oss varje morgon.
english: I have started exercising at our home every morning.

target: De har öppnat en ny restaurang väl.
english: They have opened a new restaurant I suppose.

target: Vi har beslutat att flytta hela tiden.
english: We have decided to move all the time.

target: Han har läst klart boken i helgen.
english: He has finished reading the book on the weekend.

target: Jag har talat med chefen sedan länge.
english: I have spoken with the boss for a long time.

target: Hon har tänkt på saken förra veckan.
english: She has thought about it last week.

target: Vi har försökt många gånger sedan länge.
english: We have tried many times for a long time.

target: De har lyckats hela tiden redan.
english: They have succeeded all the time already.

target: Jag har bestämt mig på morgonen nog.
english: I have made up my mind in the morning probably.

target: Vi har funnit en lösning varje dag.
english: We have found a solution every day.

target: Hon har vuxit upp i Sverige nog.
english: She has grown up in Sweden probably.

target: Han har suttit här länge efter jobbet.
english: He has been sitting here for a long time after work.
grammar: "Sitta" → "suttit." Irregular supine.

target: Jag har stått i kö i en timme.
english: I have been standing in line for an hour.

target: Vi har legat just nu väl.
english: We have been lying on the beach right now I suppose.
grammar: "Ligga" → "legat." Important: ligga = lie, lägga = lay.

target: De har hållit sitt löfte väldigt ofta.
english: They have kept their promise very often.

target: Jag har valt den blå väldigt ofta.
english: I have chosen the blue one very often.

target: Hon har burit väskan hela dagen nog.
english: She has carried the bag all day probably.

target: Vi har dragit i nödtråden ibland nog.
english: We have pulled the emergency cord sometimes probably.

target: Han har bitit sig i tungan väl.
english: He has bitten his tongue I suppose.

target: Jag har frusit hela dagen hela tiden.
english: I have been cold all day all the time.

target: Vi har slutit avtal väldigt ofta nog.
english: We have signed an agreement very often probably.

target: Hon har bundit fast båten i helgen.
english: She has tied the boat on the weekend.

target: De har stigit i pris varje dag.
english: They have risen in price every day.

target: Jag har brunnit maten under veckan alltid.
english: I have burnt the food during the week always.

target: Vi har farit illa under sommaren väl.
english: We have been harmed during the summer I suppose.

target: Han har svurit att komma väldigt ofta.
english: He has sworn to come very often.

target: Jag har aldrig flugit förut i helgen.
english: I have never flown before on the weekend.

target: Vi har redan gjort det på kvällen.
english: We have already done it in the evening.

target: Hon har precis lämnat sedan länge nog.
english: She has just left for a long time probably.

target: De har ännu inte bestämt sig nog.
english: They still haven't decided probably.

target: Jag har alltid gillat Sverige under veckan.
english: I have always liked Sweden during the week.

target: Vi har ofta undrat väldigt ofta nog.
english: We have often wondered very often probably.

target: Han har äntligen kommit nästa vecka nog.
english: He has finally arrived next week probably.

target: Jag har ibland tvekat hela tiden väl.
english: I have sometimes hesitated all the time I suppose.

target: Vi har förhoppningsvis gjort rätt förra veckan.
english: We have hopefully done the right thing last week.

target: Hon har uppenbarligen ändrat sig på kvällen.
english: She has obviously changed her mind in the evening.

target: De har tydligen glömt förra veckan också.
english: They have apparently forgotten last week too.

target: Jag har med säkerhet sett det förut.
english: I have certainly seen it before.
